comment_text.value:
The way I see it, third party applications increase the value of using twitter, bringing more users to it. Twitter as a social sharing tool has very little value to me, personally, but as a chat tool, marketing tool, or customer support tool I think it has a lot of potential. Its presentation/UX is not very optimized for those experiences, though -- and that's why third party apps exist. If an open source project builds its chatroom on top of twitter, that's a huge value-add and would bring people to use twitter in order to efficiently communicate with the company, in the same way people use Slack because companies host their support on it.

By the way, I think their rate limiting is fine for most third party apps. There is a lot that can be done with intermediate caching and the Streaming API.

We're doing the same thing on our docs pages - it's really a good way to figure out places where you need to improve.

And I hope they publish it as a client-side library as the article hints at. We needed a solutions like this recently, but had to write our own that connects to our Zendesk.

I was surprised that I found none of the customer support services that support this kind of simple feedback. In general, customer support tools need to up their game regarding client-side integration.

comment_text.value:
It makes sense to me and I'm saying this as a strong believer in AI and its ability to add value.

The system itself doesn't reward value creation. I've been saying this for years. I've seen many smart people waste their time on bureaucracy; their intelligence was being wasted; so I'm not surprised at all that now that we have AI, that its intelligence is being wasted as well.

The bottleneck is an allocation issue, not a capability issue.

The current reality is that a lot of very bright people are currently working for big tech in bureaucratic roles and not allowed to focus their attention on 'risky' problems which would deliver real value if resolved.

The current system prioritizes monopolization and is designed to try to ensure that all innovation happens within big tech. It is sacrificing potential innovation which could have occurred much faster outside of big tech in order to ensure that any gains are captured by big tech... But it's sacrificing an enormous about of efficiency.

I hope big AI companies can use their political leverage to try to open up opportunities for people who want to innovate outside of big tech. That's aligned with their long term interests.

I think AI companies are convenient structures which could allow big funds to benefit from decentralized innovation. Could create real win-win scenarios. But those AI companies have to stop pursuing the corporate and government money and prioritize small customers and support small tool makers (or at least lobby the government to stop hindering them with regulations). Also, bootstrapping should be prioritized because VC money mostly creates moats.

story_title.value: AI delivers 'zero financial payoff' to most companies, Apollo economist says

comment_text.value: Hi HN - OP here. We've been developing customer support tools for mobile apps for a while now (mostly live chat), and we've noticed that most apps bump you into an email form when you have a support query, or mobile browser for their FAQ. So we decided to build a Helpdesk that lives inside your app - lets your users see and search the FAQ right inside your app, imports your content from Desk/Zendesk, lets users open tickets also inside the app, and alerts them with answers using push notifications. Happy to answer any questions, and totally open to suggestions!

story_title.value: Show HN: Lightningdesk - Real-time native in-app Helpdesk for iOS/Android apps
